findings.evidence: The theorem rewrites `mapValue f (aeval φ p)` strictly toward `aeval (mapValue f φ) (p.map f.toRingHom)`, matching the normal-form role already given to `mapValue_algebraMap` at line 185.
findings.issue: `mapValue_aeval` is the characteristic polynomial-evaluation rule but lacks `@[simp]`, so scalar extension does not normalize through `aeval`.

findings.evidence: `semisimplePart_prodMap`, `unipotentPart_prodMap`, `semisimplePart_tensorProduct`, `unipotentPart_tensorProduct`, and the `congrLinearEquiv` component formulas are all confirmed `@[simp]` rules.
findings.issue: The parallel `semisimplePart_mapValue` and `unipotentPart_mapValue` formulas lack `@[simp]`, unlike the existing product, tensor-product, and linear-equivalence factor formulas.

findings.evidence: `JordanDecomposition/Naturality.lean` lines 89, 117, and 126 provide exactly these normalized simp forms for `jordanDecomposition_mapDomain`, `semisimplePart_mapDomain`, and `unipotentPart_mapDomain`; `AlgHom.mapValue_apply` similarly normalizes the new surface.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` restatements for the Jordan pair and both components using `toConv (f.comp g.ofConv)`, analogous to the existing map-domain `*_toConv_comp` lemmas.
findings.issue: The point-level map-value formulas have no simp-normalized forms after `AlgHom.mapValue_apply`, leaving all three decomposition/component naturality formulas unavailable to `simp`.

summary: The scalar-extension API omits normal-form automation for its central evaluation and Jordan-factor formulas.
